answer: A deposit that only unlocks after a long history of useful work raises the cost of fake identities. Think of reputation as a glacier: it grows slowly and melts fast when an agent misbehaves. A prism of checks, stake, past trades, and peer ratings, splits one signal into several views, so a single bought account cannot fake them all. Even a violet flag from one check forces a review before the agent can trade again. An attacker must pay the deposit, wait months, and still pass every view, which makes bulk sybil creation too slow and too expensive to pay off.
